main_text.p: etiam linguam ipsam tradiderūt.Postea a judæis coepta est figuris Hebraicis scribi: qui jam a M,annis,& suprà,tefte Munstero,Chaldaicas translationes & expositiones aliter non habuerunt.

COLCHIS lingua eadem est, quæ Ægyptiis.] Hariolantur enim vetustissimus ille & optimus scriptor Herodotus,atque alii præterea Græci,Colchos ab Ægyptiis originem ducere:ut propterea μετηλυδας αιγυπτιοι eos vocarit Dionys. ὀπισθηγητης quod tribus fere conjecturis probare nititur: primâ, a coloris atri, & capillorum crisporum similitudine: secundâ, a Circumcisionis ritu, quem ad ætatem usqu fuam retinuerint: tertiâ, a sacrificii & linguæ communione. Verum ob has ipsas conjecturas, vel plerasque certè, Israelitarum potius, quos ex decem tribus a Salmanassaro, Assyriorum Imp. in Colchos & Iberos traductos,ex sacris libris constat, propaginem esse Colchos videtur. Colchi enim totidem & iisdem litteris a scriptura vocantur:& Circumcisionis ceremonia a judæis, non Ægyptiis primò professa est: & ater fuscusque color etiamnum hodie judæis non insolens est.
CORALLI,] Populi Pontici,flumen Istrum & Rhodopem, montemque Æmum

page.notes: Catchword reads "adco" at the foot right, partly cut off; given as "adco." Several Greek words in the Dionysius and Herodotus passage are only partly legible in the scan (μετηλυδας, αιγυπτιοι, ὀπισθηγητης); transcribed from the visible letters with doubt; the Greek accents are uncertain. Words "ufq;" read as usque with abbreviation as printed. Line "Istrum" is partly obscured by a stain. The last line is a catchword-like fragment and is also the final text line; "adco" stays as the catchword. Printed "tradiderūt" shows a macron as printed. Several words in the second paragraph are uncertain and should be checked: "Hariolantur", "Dionys.", "Munstero", "Salmanassaro".
